etymology_text:
From Koine Greek δεκατρία (dekatría). By surface analysis, δέκα (déka, “ten”) + τρία (tría, “three”).
Cognate with Mariupol Greek дъэкатри́я (ðekatríja), дъекатри́я (ðjekatríja).
From μισός (misós, “half”), from Byzantine Greek ἥμισος (hḗmisos, “half”), from Ancient Greek ἥμισυς (hḗmisus, “half”).

examples.text: μισό κιλό κρασί
examples.translation: half a kilo of wine
examples.english: half a kilo of wine

related.english: one half of a game, half-time
related.translation: one half of a game, half-time

etymology_text: Inherited from Byzantine Greek σαράντα (saránta), from Ancient Greek τεσσαράκοντα (tessarákonta), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwr̥̄ḱomt, from earlier *kʷetwr̥-dḱomt (“four-ten”). The first three letters were mistaken for the article τὲς (tès, “the”, feminine accusative plural) in Medieval times, hence the loss. The memorial service is derived from the belief that Jesus Christ was resurrected for that period of time before ascending to Heaven.
